reading.body:
Capitol Counsel's AI lobbying is concentrated in electric power and health care, not in the technology firms usually associated with AI policy.

The largest client by AI filings is the Edison Electric Institute, with 10. The Healthcare Leadership Council follows at 6, then Baxter Healthcare at 3 and Intuit at 2. That ordering matters for AI specifically: the trade group for investor-owned utilities is the single biggest source of this firm's AI lobbying volume, which puts grid and power interests at the front of the client list rather than at the margins. Health care clients account for 9 filings between them, a reminder that AI governance questions reach sectors that are regulated for safety and privacy rather than for software.

The work is spread across a large roster. Twenty-two lobbyists are named on these filings, and no single person dominates: Shannon Finley appears on 17, Jeffrey Carroll on 13, and Joseph Eannello and David Olander on 12 each, with a long tail of names on one or two filings. Six bills are named in filings from 2025 or later, four in the Senate and two in the House. The data does not include the text of those bills, the positions the firm argued, or which client each bill touches, so the specific policy stakes cannot be read from this page.

What the data covers is disclosure, not influence. A filing records that a client lobbied on an AI issue, not what it sought. The counts here measure how often AI appears in this firm's registered activity, and nothing about outcomes, spending, or whether any bill moved.
